A: The first line must start with a severity tag in square brackets, one of `[blocker]`, `[major]`, `[minor]`, `[nit]`, followed by a short title.
Propose the change on a line that starts with `Proposed fix: `.
Give the place in the code on its own line as `Location: <file>:<line>`.
Give the outcome on a line `Verdict: approve`, `Verdict: request changes` or `Verdict: comment`.
State every finding as a statement. A question mark may appear only on a final line that starts with `Open question:`.
Say how sure you are on a line `Confidence: high`, `Confidence: medium` or `Confidence: low`.
B: Ask the author at least one clarifying question, written as a full sentence that ends with a question mark.
Classify the comment on a line `Category: correctness`, `Category: security`, `Category: performance`, `Category: readability` or `Category: testing`.
The first line must be plain text of the form `Review: <title>`, with no tag or bracket before it.
Name one good thing about the diff on a line that starts with `What works well: `.
Close your assessment with a separate line that reads `Verdict: approve`, `Verdict: request changes` or `Verdict: comment`.
Estimate the work needed on a line `Effort: S`, `Effort: M` or `Effort: L`.

relations.reason: Skill A requires a severity tag in square brackets, while Skill B requires plain text without any tags or brackets.

Skill A requires the proposed fix to be on a line that starts with 'Proposed fix: ', while Skill B requires a good thing about the diff to be on a line that starts with 'What works well: '. These lines cannot be the same.
Skill A requires the location to be on its own line, while Skill B requires at least one clarifying question. These cannot be on the same line.
Both skills require a verdict, but the format is different.
Skill A requires every finding to be a statement, while Skill B requires a category. These cannot be on the same line.
Skill A requires confidence to be on its own line, while Skill B requires effort to be on its own line. These cannot be on the same line.

reconciled: Name one good thing about the diff on a line that starts with `What works well: ` and propose the change on a line that starts with `Proposed fix: `, by placing the proposed change immediately after the line that starts with `What works well: ` and starting the proposed change on a new line.
Write the author's response to the clarifying question on the same line as the question, followed by `Location: <file>:<line>` on a new line.

Classify the comment on a line as one of the following categories: `Category: correctness`, `Category: security`, `Category: performance`, `Category: readability`, or `Category: testing`. State every finding as a statement, and if there are multiple findings, end with a line that starts with `Open question:`.

Estimate the work needed on a line as `Effort: S` if the task is straightforward and requires minimal effort, `Effort: M` if the task is moderately complex and requires some effort, or `Effort: L` if the task is complex and requires significant effort. Express your confidence in the assessment as `Confidence: high` if you are very sure, `Confidence: medium` if you are somewhat sure, or `Confidence: low` if you are not very sure.
